title: Sigeumchi Namul Seasoned Spinach
shortDescription: Spinach is briefly blanched, cooled, squeezed, and gently seasoned with garlic, soy sauce, toasted sesame oil, scallion, and sesame seeds.
culturalContext: Sigeumchi namul is a familiar Korean vegetable banchan and a common component of meals and bibimbap. Seasoning can be soy-based or salt-based and may include doenjang; this draft uses a restrained soy-sesame profile.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

ingredients.preparation: washed thoroughly, tough root ends trimmed

instructions.heading: Wash and trim
instructions.action: Wash spinach in repeated changes of cool water until no grit remains. Trim only tough root ends, keeping tender stems attached.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The final rinse water is clear and leaves look fresh, not slimy.
instructions.safetyNote: Discard slimy or spoiled leaves and use a clean sink and bowl.

instructions.heading: Prepare water
instructions.action: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil, add the blanching salt, and prepare a separate bowl of cold water.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Water boils vigorously before spinach is added.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep pot handles turned inward and lower spinach away from your body to avoid splashes.

instructions.heading: Blanch
instructions.action: Add spinach stems first, then leaves. Press under the water with tongs and blanch 45 to 60 seconds until uniformly wilted and vivid green.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Leaves are bright green and collapsed while stems remain tender.
instructions.safetyNote: Use clean tongs and avoid overfilling the pot.

instructions.heading: Cool and squeeze
instructions.action: Transfer immediately to cold water, swish, drain, and squeeze gently in small handfuls. Cut the squeezed bundle into 5 cm / 2-inch lengths.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Spinach is cool, moist but not dripping, and separates easily.
instructions.safetyNote: Use potable water and clean hands or gloves when handling the cooked spinach.

instructions.heading: Season
instructions.action: Loosen spinach in a clean bowl. Add soy sauce, garlic, sesame oil, scallion, and sesame seeds; mix gently by hand or with clean tongs.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Every strand is lightly glossy without a pool of dressing.
instructions.safetyNote: Declare soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame allergens.

instructions.heading: Serve or chill
instructions.action: Taste only after mixing with clean utensils. Serve promptly or refrigerate in a shallow covered container.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Spinach stays bright green and tender rather than mushy.
instructions.safetyNote: Refrigerate within 2 hours at or below 40°F / 4°C.

grillSetup: Not applicable; this banchan is blanched on the stovetop.
visualDonenessCues: Spinach is vivid green and uniformly wilted
Seasoned leaves are moist but not watery
foodSafetyNotes: Wash spinach thoroughly to remove grit and discard spoiled leaves.
Use potable cold water and clean tools after blanching.
Avoid leaving cooked spinach at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
Refrigerate at or below 40°F / 4°C in a shallow covered container.
Declare soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame allergens.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame; use verified tamari for a gluten-free adaptation and prevent shared-utensil cross-contact.

substitutions: Use certified gluten-free tamari for soy sauce only after checking the full label.
Baby spinach cooks faster and needs a separately tested blanch time.
ingredientSourcing: Choose spinach with crisp leaves and tender stems, avoiding slimy bags.
Korean soup soy sauce may be evaluated in testing as a saltier alternative to regular soy sauce.
makeAhead: Blanch, cool, and squeeze spinach up to 1 day ahead; refrigerate covered and season closer to serving.
storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days; texture and color are best earlier and the limit requires food-safety review.
reheating: Serve cold or cool; if warming, heat briefly in a covered skillet and do not repeatedly cool and reheat.
leftovers: Use properly refrigerated leftovers in bibimbap or a rice bowl within the approved storage window.
servingSuggestions: Serve as a small banchan with rice
Use as one component of bibimbap

faq.question: Why cool spinach after blanching?
faq.answer: Cooling stops carryover cooking and helps preserve bright color and a tender, distinct texture.

faq.question: How dry should the spinach be?
faq.answer: Squeeze out free water without crushing the stems; the spinach should remain moist but not dilute the seasoning.
